In summary, our research is concerned with
the long-time dynamics of non-equilibrium critical systems, which is an important problem in nonequilibrium statistical physics.
the response of systems with long-range correlations, and with the effects of the initial conditions on the long-time dynamics.
the response of non-equilibrium statistical systems to a change in their environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the long-time dynamics of non-conserved systems is not universal.
the long-time dynamics of this model is non-trivial, and is controlled by the initial state.
the non-equilibrium dynamics of the spherical model is completely determined by the form of the long-range initial correlations, and that this is the case for all temperatures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the long-time dynamics of non-equilibrium spherical model is rich, and that the long-range correlations of the initial state can have a significant impact on its long-time dynamics.
the long-time behaviour of a non-equilibrium system depends on the details of its initial conditions, even in the absence of disorder.
the initial conditions play a crucial role in the ageing dynamics of the spherical model, and that the two-time autocorrlation and autoresponse functions are generically different from each other.
The main takeaway from our work is that
non-equilibrium dynamics is generically non-thermal.
the long-time dynamics of systems out of equilibrium depends on the initial correlations and not only on the initial temperature.

, contrary to what is often assumed, the long-time dynamics of a system with long-range initial conditions cannot be described by the same scaling functions as for a system prepared at the infinite-temperature state.
